//! A package of held files for the program layer's tests: an in-memory source world, its files
//! addressed in one package, a prelude beside it, and a store of its own for each case.
use core.{distinct}
use @std.io.{make_dirs}
use @std.program.address.{DirectoryAddress, SourceFileAddress}
use @std.time.{stamp}

/// The files the world holds, by their path in the package.
export once fn files() -> Cell<Map<string, string>> {
    let held: Map<string, string> = {}
    Cell.new(held)
}

/// A held file's text, absent for one not held.
export fn read_held(file: SourceFileAddress) -> string? { files().get().get(file.path_in_package) }

/// A directory's names: the held files directly in it, and the directories holding the rest.
export fn list_held(dir: DirectoryAddress) -> List<string>? {
    let prefix = if dir.path_in_package.is_empty() { "" } else { "${dir.path_in_package}/" }
    let under = [path.substring(prefix.length, path.length) for path in files().get().keys() if path.starts_with(prefix)]
    if under.is_empty() { return null }
    distinct(
        [if rest.contains("/") { rest.substring(0, rest.index_of("/")) } else { rest } for rest in under],
    )
}

    let dir = "/tmp/avra-program-test/${stamp()}/${name}"
    let _ = make_dirs(dir)
    dir
}

// THE IR PROOF: an alpha-renamed comparison of the enclosing
// declaration's own lowering, before and after — PROVED for a
// rewrite that changes nothing about what the program does (a
// negated condition with its arms swapped, `core.canon_not_if`'s own
// case), REFUSED for a text that merely LOOKS like the same shape
// but changes an operator's meaning.
use @std.avrac.testing.old_path.{test_workspace}
use @std.avrac.compiler.{Program, Workspace, Analysis}
use @std.avrac.compiler.host.{memory_host}
use @std.avrac.core.{
    At,
    Ins,
    Reg,
    UnOp,
    BinOp,
    alpha_fps,
    alpha_renamed,
    same_fps,
    same_ins_list,
    fp_str,
}
use @std.avrac.features.{Analysed}
use @std.errors.{Edit, Loc}

fn proof_ws_of(main: string) -> Workspace {
    test_workspace(memory_host({"/w/src/main.av": main}, ["/w/src/main.av"]), "/w")
}

fn analysed_of(a: Analysis) -> Analysed {
    Analysed { view: a.view, names: a.names, facts: a.facts }
}

fn root_at(a: Analysis) -> At {
    At.Stmt(a.view.stmts.first()!)
}

/// An edit over the FIRST occurrence of `needle` in `text` — the
/// generalized proof's own callers have no node id, only a byte

fn warm(before: Map<string, string>, after: Map<string, string>) -> string {

/// The report of `after` read off the bytes a check of `before` saved on disk.

    warm(before, after) == cold && warm_on_disk(before, after) == cold && cold.contains(words)
}

```
#!/bin/sh
# `avra fix` SAYS AND WRITES ON THE PROGRAM LAYER WHAT IT DOES ON THE OLD PATH. Each case under
# tools/program-fixes/ is a package of its own (tools/lib/cases.sh), copied cold for each path. Held
# alike, word for word: `fix --dry --json` (each application, its tier — proved, accepted by its
# rule's law, repaired, or only shown — and its edits), the same under `--repair`, and the file
# `fix` writes. A case holding `differs.why` is known to differ for the reason written there: said,
# not failed, while it differs, and failed once it holds.
#   sh tools/witness_program_fixes.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra, every case)
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
. "$root/tools/lib/cases.sh"
cases_dir="$root/tools/program-fixes"
avra=${1:-build/avra}
case $avra in /*) ;; *) avra="$root/$avra" ;; esac
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "witness_program_fixes: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'find "$tmp" -delete' EXIT
# what `fix` says and writes of the case `$1` on the path `$2` (0 the old, 1 the program layer), its
# copy's path said as `<case>`
said() {
    c="$tmp/$1.$2"
    cp -R "$cases_dir/$1" "$c"
    find "$c" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \;
    mkdir -p "$c.store"
    for flags in "--dry --json" "--dry --json --repair"; do
        (cd "$c" && AVRA_PROGRAM=$2 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$c.store" "$avra" fix $flags . >"$c.said" 2>/dev/null)
        code=$?
        sed "s#$c#<case>#g" "$c.said"
        echo "exit $code"
avra.toml
differs.why
src
Shell cwd was reset to /home/user
```

//! A STORE LAYERED OVER A SHARED ONE: a package's own store over the machine's, where the answers
//! every package built by this binary can share are kept once. A question is read in its own store,
//! then in the shared one; a SHARED question — one whose every input lies in a package the shared
//! store serves, and whose every read is shared — is kept in the shared store, every other in its
//! own. Where each package's sources stand is the store's to say: a path lies in the package whose
//! root holds it most nearly. Nothing is reused that its record doesn't still hold, wherever the record lies, so a question

/// Whether `a` and `b` hold the same prints in the same order.
fn same_prints(a: List<int>, b: List<int>) -> bool { a.length == b.length && (0..a.length).all(a[it] == b[it]) }

    match b.view { .Verbatim(stmts, _) -> stmts, rest -> [] }
}

/// WHETHER A FILE STANDS CANONICAL: its text printed back is its text, byte for byte. The answer is

/// providers nobody edited, is not parsed or printed again.
@query
export fn file_canonical(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> Canonical {
    match file_formatted(engine, file) {
        .Ok(text) -> if "${text}\n" == source_text(engine, file) ?? "" { Canonical.Stands } else { Canonical.Differs },
        .Err(report) -> Canonical.Refused(report.split("\n").first() ?? report),
    }
}

// A file's `// LICENSED` citations that name nothing, as the program layer's check refuses them:
// an id no rule carries and no keeper's family holds is stale; a rule's id and a family's member
// are not; a citation's words inside a string are no comment at all.
use compiler.{StaleCitation, avra_fact_definitions, stale_citations}
use @std.avrac.testing.held.{empty_store, held_at}
use @std.program.query_engine.{query_engine}

/// The stale citations of `src/main.av` holding `main`, in a package of its own.
fn stale_in(main: string) -> List<StaleCitation> {
    let held = held_at(
        {"/c/avra.toml": "[package]\nname = \"cited\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n", "/c/src/main.av": main},
        "/c",
    )
    held.entered()
    stale_citations(query_engine(empty_store(), avra_fact_definitions()), held.file_at("/c/src/main.av"))
}

spec "stale `// LICENSED` citations on the program layer" {
    given "a citation naming no rule" {
        then "it is stale, at its own line, by its id" {
            let found = stale_in("fn f() -> int { 1 }\n// LICENSED style.no_such_rule: nothing backs it\nf()\n")
            found.length == 1 && found[0].line == 2 && found[0].id == "style.no_such_rule"
        }
    }
    given "a rule's own id and a keeper's family member" {
        then "neither is stale" {
            stale_in("// LICENSED loops.push_loop: a rule\n// LICENSED input.clock: a keeper's\nfn f() -> int { 1 }\nf()\n")
                .is_empty()
        }
    }
    given "a citation's words inside a string" {
        then "nothing is stale: a string is no comment" {
            stale_in("fn f() -> string { \"// LICENSED style.no_such_rule: in a string\" }\nf()\n").is_empty()
        }
    }
    given "a bare doctrine exemption with no id" {
        then "it claims nothing, so nothing is stale" {
            stale_in("// LICENSED — a doctrine exemption\nfn f() -> int { 1 }\nf()\n").is_empty()
        }
    }
}

file_path: /work/avra/packages/cli/src/commands/std_answers.av
--- content ---
//! THE TOOLCHAIN'S STD ANSWERS: an installed toolchain ships, beside its std, the packs its own
//! binary kept over that std (`make install`), so a program's first build works out none of std.
//! They are laid into the machine's store once per binary, each pack published whole, so a reader
//! sees a pack or none; a binary of another print never reads them, and every answer is held to the
//! inputs it read wherever it was kept. A machine store that can't take them, or can't stand at
//! all, is said once, and the build works without it.
use @std.io.{IoError, drafted, exists, make_dirs, read_bytes}
use @std.path.{dir_of, joined_path}
use @std.program.disk_store.{packs_answering}

/// Where the toolchain beside this binary keeps its std answers: `<prefix>/lib/avra/answers`, a
/// sibling of its std.
fn shipped_answers() -> string? {
    let bin? = own_binary() else { return null }
    joined_path(dir_of(dir_of(bin)), "lib/avra/answers")
}

/// Whether the machine's store at `directory` stands for this process: made where it isn't, said
/// once where it can't be.
fn machine_store_stands(directory: string) -> bool {
    match make_dirs(directory) {
        .Ok(_) -> true,
        .Err(e) -> {
            said_once(store_unusable(directory, e))
            false
        },
    }
}

/// The toolchain's std answers for the binary printed `print`, laid into the machine's store at
/// `directory` once: each pack it ships that the store lacks, then the mark that they were.
fn std_answers_laid(directory: string, print: string) {
    let shipped? = shipped_answers() else { return }
    let packs = packs_answering(shipped, print)
    if packs.is_empty() { return }
    let mark = joined_path(directory, "std-answers-${print}")
    if exists(mark) { return }
    for name in packs {
        match pack_laid(joined_path(shipped, name), joined_path(directory, name)) {
            .Ok(_) -> {},
            .Err(e) -> {
                said_once(answers_unlaid(directory, e))
                return
            },
        }
    }
    let _ = file_laid(mark, "".bytes())
}

/// The pack at `from` laid at `to`, unless one stands there.
fn pack_laid(from: string, to: string) -> Result<string, IoError> {
    if exists(to) { return .Ok(to) }
    file_laid(to, read_bytes(from)?)
}

/// `bytes` published whole at `to`: a reader sees the file or none.
fn file_laid(to: string, bytes: Bytes) -> Result<string, IoError> {
    let draft = drafted(to)?
    match draft.write(bytes) {
        .Ok(_) -> draft.published(to),
        .Err(e) -> {
            draft.dropped()
            .Err(e)
        },
    }
}

/// Whether this process has said why it works without the machine's store.
once fn said_store() -> Cell<bool> { Cell.new(false) }

/// `words` on stderr, the first time this process says why the machine's store doesn't serve it.
fn said_once(words: string) {
    if said_store().get() { return }
    said_store().set(true)
    eprintln("avra: ${words}")
}

fn store_unusable(directory: string, e: IoError) -> string {
    "the machine's store at ${directory} can't stand (${e.describe()}), so this build shares nothing across packages"
}

fn answers_unlaid(directory: string, e: IoError) -> string {
    "the toolchain's std answers couldn't be laid in ${directory} (${e.describe()}), so this build works std out itself"
}

file_path: /work/avra/tools/std_answers.sh
--- content ---
#!/bin/sh
# THE TOOLCHAIN'S STD ANSWERS: the compiler `avra` checks every std package under `std` with the
# machine's store placed at `out`, so `out` holds the packs that compiler keeps over that std — what a
# program's first build reads instead of working std out (cli's std_answers.av lays them in). Run by
# the INSTALLED compiler over the INSTALLED std, so the packs are made at the paths and the print a
# program is built with. Each package's own store is left behind nowhere: it is made under a scratch
# cache and emptied. Prints one line: how many packages, how many packs, how many kilobytes.
#   sh tools/std_answers.sh <avra> <std> <out>
set -u
[ $# -eq 3 ] || { sed -n 2,8p "$0"; exit 2; }
avra=$1; std=$2; out=$3
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "std_answers: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$std" ] || { echo "std_answers: no std at $std" >&2; exit 1; }
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'find "$scratch" -delete' EXIT
mkdir -p "$out"
find "$out" -mindepth 1 -delete
n=0
for p in "$std"/std-*; do
    [ -f "$p/avra.toml" ] || continue
    AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$scratch" AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR="$out" AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 "$avra" check "$p" >/dev/null 2>"$scratch/said" ||
        { echo "std_answers: $(basename "$p") is refused by its own compiler:" >&2; cat "$scratch/said" >&2; exit 1; }
    find "$p" -name .avra-cache -type d -prune -exec find {} -delete \;
    n=$((n + 1))
done
find "$out" -mindepth 1 ! -name 'pack-*' -delete
echo "std answers: $n packages, $(ls "$out" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') packs, $(du -sk "$out" | cut -f1) KB in $out"

#!/bin/sh
# THE TOOLCHAIN'S STD ANSWERS SERVE A PROGRAM'S FIRST CHECK, AND NEVER WRONGLY. A toolchain is laid
# out as `make install` lays one (bin/avra, lib/avra/std, lib/avra/answers), shipping the answers its
# compiler keeps over @std/text, and a program over @std/text is checked against it:
#   (1) on a fresh machine, the shipped packs are laid in, and the check says what a check with no
#       machine store says, its own store holding less than half of what that one's does;
#   (2) two first checks at once on one fresh machine both say it, and leave every pack whole and
#       no draft behind;
#   (3) a compiler of another print lays nothing in;
#   (4) a machine store that can't stand, or a disk too small for the packs (where this machine can
#       mount one), costs one line on stderr and nothing else: the check says what it says without.
#   sh tools/std_answers_attack.sh [compiler]     (default build/avra-try)
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
avra=$(cd "$(dirname "${1:-$root/build/avra-try}")" && pwd)/$(basename "${1:-$root/build/avra-try}")
w=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/avra-std-answers.XXXXXX")
mounted=""
trap '[ -n "$mounted" ] && umount "$mounted" 2>/dev/null; find "$w" -delete 2>/dev/null || :' EXIT
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
unset AVRA_MACHINE_STORE AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR
fail() { echo "std_answers_attack: $*"; exit 1; }
held() { echo "std_answers_attack: $*"; }

tc="$w/tc"
mkdir -p "$tc/bin" "$tc/lib/avra"
cp "$avra" "$tc/bin/avra"
ln -s "$root/packages" "$tc/lib/avra/std"
sh "$root/tools/std_answers.sh" "$tc/bin/avra" "$tc/lib/avra/std" "$tc/lib/avra/answers" std-text >/dev/null ||
    fail "the toolchain's answers were not made"
shipped=$(ls "$tc/lib/avra/answers" | grep -c '^pack-')
[ "$shipped" -gt 0 ] || fail "the toolchain ships no pack"

mkdir -p "$w/p/src"
printf '[package]\nname = "texted"\nversion = "0.0.1"\n' > "$w/p/avra.toml"
printf 'use @std.text.{parse_int}\n\nfn n() -> int { parse_int("41") ?? 0 }\nn()\n' > "$w/p/src/main.av"
own_emptied() { find "$w/p" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \; ; }
# `checked <compiler> <cache> <said> [env…]`: the program checked cold in its own store, under the
# machine cache `<cache>`; stdout to `<said>`, stderr to `<said>.err`, the exit after stdout
checked() {
    c=$1; cache=$2; said=$3; shift 3
    own_emptied
    env AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" "$@" "$c" check "$w/p" > "$said" 2> "$said.err"
    echo "exit $?" >> "$said"
}

checked "$tc/bin/avra" "$w/none" "$w/cold" AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=0
cold_own=$(du -sk "$w/p/.avra-cache" | cut -f1)

# (1)
checked "$tc/bin/avra" "$w/m1" "$w/laid"
cmp -s "$w/cold" "$w/laid" || fail "(1) the check over the laid-in answers says otherwise: $(cat "$w/laid" "$w/laid.err")"
[ ! -s "$w/laid.err" ] || fail "(1) a first check said: $(cat "$w/laid.err")"
laid_own=$(du -sk "$w/p/.avra-cache" | cut -f1)
[ $((laid_own * 2)) -lt "$cold_own" ] || fail "(1) the own store holds ${laid_own} KB against ${cold_own} cold: the shipped answers didn't serve"
held "(1) laid in on a fresh machine: the same words, own store ${laid_own} KB against ${cold_own} KB cold"

# (2)
for k in 1 2; do (checked "$tc/bin/avra" "$w/m2" "$w/race$k") & done
wait
for k in 1 2; do cmp -s "$w/cold" "$w/race$k" || fail "(2) racer $k says otherwise: $(cat "$w/race$k" "$w/race$k.err")"; done
ls "$w/m2/tapes" | grep -q 'draft$' && fail "(2) a draft is left: $(ls "$w/m2/tapes")"
for n in $(ls "$tc/lib/avra/answers"); do cmp -s "$tc/lib/avra/answers/$n" "$w/m2/tapes/$n" || [ ! -e "$w/m2/tapes/$n" ] || fail "(2) pack $n lies torn"; done
held "(2) two first checks at once: the same words, no draft, every pack whole"

# (3)
cp "$avra" "$w/other-avra"
printf 'another print' >> "$w/other-avra"
mkdir -p "$w/tc2/bin" "$w/tc2/lib/avra"
cp "$w/other-avra" "$w/tc2/bin/avra"
ln -s "$root/packages" "$w/tc2/lib/avra/std"
ln -s "$tc/lib/avra/answers" "$w/tc2/lib/avra/answers"
checked "$w/tc2/bin/avra" "$w/m3" "$w/other"
cmp -s "$w/cold" "$w/other" || fail "(3) the other compiler says otherwise: $(cat "$w/other" "$w/other.err")"
for n in $(ls "$tc/lib/avra/answers"); do [ ! -e "$w/m3/tapes/$n" ] || fail "(3) a compiler of another print laid in $n"; done
held "(3) a compiler of another print laid nothing in"

# (4)
touch "$w/a-file"
checked "$tc/bin/avra" "$w/m4" "$w/unstood" AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR="$w/a-file/tapes"
cmp -s "$w/cold" "$w/unstood" || fail "(4) a check whose machine store can't stand says otherwise: $(cat "$w/unstood")"
[ "$(wc -l < "$w/unstood.err")" -eq 1 ] && grep -q "can't stand" "$w/unstood.err" ||
    fail "(4) a machine store that can't stand is said otherwise: $(cat "$w/unstood.err")"
held "(4) a machine store that can't stand: one line, the same words"
mkdir -p "$w/tiny"
if mount -t tmpfs -o size=64k tmpfs "$w/tiny" 2>/dev/null; then
    mounted="$w/tiny"
    checked "$tc/bin/avra" "$w/m5" "$w/full" AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR="$w/tiny/tapes"
    cmp -s "$w/cold" "$w/full" || fail "(4) a check on a full disk says otherwise: $(cat "$w/full")"
    [ "$(grep -c "couldn't be laid" "$w/full.err")" -eq 1 ] || fail "(4) a full disk is said otherwise: $(cat "$w/full.err")"
    held "(4) a disk too small for the packs: one line, the same words"
else
    held "(4) a full disk: not attacked, this machine mounts no small disk"
fi
echo "std_answers_attack: held"

```
#!/bin/sh
# A BUILD ANSWERS BEFORE ITS STORE IS SAVED, AND THE NEXT BUILD READS THE SAVE WHOLE. A build
# leaves its store to an heir, a process that outlives it. One package, its heir held back
# (`AVRA_HEIR_LINGERS_MS`) so each case meets the save unfinished:
#   a build started at once says it waits for the heir, then stands on what it saved, working out
#   nothing;
#   an heir killed before it saves costs the next build its work and never its answer, and that
#   build says the save did not finish, once;
#   a store emptied under the heir is built again whole;
#   an edit made while the heir saves is the edit the next build builds;
#   `AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE` saves before the build answers, and leaves no heir.
#
#   sh tools/heir_save_attack.sh
set -u
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/attack.sh"
A=${HEIR_ATTACK_AVRA:-$(pwd)/avra}
R=build/heir-save-attack
find "$R" -delete 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p "$R"
unset AVRA_PROGRAM AVRA_PROGRAM_NET AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_HEIR_LINGERS_MS
LINGER=4000

# The package `$1`: an entry printing `word()` and the sum of enough files that a cold build forks.
package() {
    p=$R/$1
    find "$p" -delete 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p "$p/src"
    printf '[package]\nname = "heir-%s"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n' "$1" > "$p/avra.toml"
    printf 'export fn word() -> string { "before" }\n' > "$p/src/leaf.av"
    uses=""; sum="0"
    for k in $(seq 0 39); do
        printf 'export fn f%s() -> int { %s }\n' "$k" "$k" > "$p/src/f$k.av"
        uses="${uses}use f$k.{f$k}\n"; sum="$sum + f$k()"
    done
    printf "use leaf.{word}\n${uses}\nprintln(\"\${word()} \${$sum}\")\n" > "$p/src/main.av"
    own_store "$p"
}

now_ms() { echo $(($(date +%s%N) / 1000000)); }
store() { echo "$R/$1/.avra-cache/tapes"; }
frontiers() { ls "$(store "$1")" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^frontier-'; }
heirs() { pgrep -f "build $R/$1\$" | wc -l | tr -d ' '; }

# THE FLOOR OF AN ATTACK, sourced after `set -u` (`. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/attack.sh"`): stands in the
# tree's root, runs under the lock its caller holds (no second watchdog) and takes no compile slot.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
export AVRA_WATCH_HELD=1
# A cold run clears the tree's `.avra-cache`; the machine store lives there too, or "cold" would read the machine's rows.
export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$PWD/.avra-cache"
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
export AVRA_MAX_COMPILES=0
fails=0
steps=0

# Marks a fixture directory as a checkout whose store is its own, cold, never the tree's.
own_store() {
    : > "$1/.git"
    export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$PWD/$1/.avra-cache"
}

# One failed check, counted and named.
fail() {
    fails=$((fails + 1))
    echo "FAIL  $*"
}

# The attack's last line — what it ran, then how much failed — and its status.
verdict() {
    echo "$1: $2, $fails failed"
    [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]
}

Prebuilt std answers are in, and the gate passes. One decision is still open: the shipped answers for the full std come to 1.09 GB. That's yours or the lead's call, and I've asked the lead.

**What changed (2e56e49f)**
- **The shared std store is now on by default.** `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=0` turns it off.
- **`make install` ships std answers.** The installed compiler checks the installed std and saves the results under `lib/avra/answers`.
- **First use per compiler build copies them in.** They go into `~/.avra/cache/tapes` once per compiler build, each file written whole. A different compiler build never picks them up.
- **Failures degrade.** If the store can't be created, or the disk is too small, you get one line on stderr and the build carries on without it.
- **A bug fixed on the way.** When the cache directory sat inside the package, the shared store and the package's own store were the same folder. That stopped a build from saving its store in the background after it answers (heir_save_attack failed). A shared store in that same folder is now ignored.

**Measured** from a real `make install` into a scratch prefix, starting with an empty package store:

| program | command | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| uses `@std.json` | check | 5.7 s | 0.59 s |
| uses `@std.json` | build | 6.1 s | 0.79 s |
| hello-world | check | 45 ms | 33 ms |
| hello-world | build | ~200 ms | ~200 ms |

The very first use on a machine pays about 2.6 s once to copy the answers in.

**Checks.** `tools/std_answers_attack.sh` is now a gate row (in the witness-b slice) and covers:
- the same output whether the shipped answers are used or not;
- two first checks racing on a fresh machine: no leftover partial files, every copied file intact;
- a different compiler build copying nothing in;
- an unusable store directory, and a tiny 64 KB disk: one line each, same output.

Separately, by hand: three rounds of two simultaneous first builds gave binaries byte-identical to builds made without the store. All 12 gate slices I ran pass on 2e56e49f.

**Decision needed: what to ship.** The 1.09 GB breaks down as std-avrac 567 MB (the compiler's own source, packaged as std), std-ui 267 MB, std-http 149 MB, std-program 112 MB. xz compresses these files about 6.4×. I'd leave out std-avrac and the test-harness packages, then measure again and add compression only if it's still large. `std_answers.sh` already takes a list of packages, so that's a small change.

5	# the INSTALLED compiler over the INSTALLED std, so the packs are made at the paths and the print a

7	# cache and emptied. Prints one line: how many packages, how many packs, how many kilobytes.

9	set -u

```
# fuzz, soak and gallery packages are its harnesses, never a program's import. Prints one line: how
# many packages, how many packs, how many kilobytes.
#   sh tools/std_answers.sh <avra> <std> <out> [package…]   (default every std package but those)
set -u
[ $# -ge 3 ] || { sed -n 2,8p "$0"; exit 2; }
avra=$1; std=$2; out=$3
shift 3
named="$*"
# the compiler's own packages, never a program's import
COMPILERS=" std-avrac std-http-fuzz std-http-soak std-ui_gallery "
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "std_answers: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$std" ] || { echo "std_answers: no std at $std" >&2; exit 1; }
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'find "$scratch" -delete' EXIT
mkdir -p "$out"
find "$out" -mindepth 1 -delete
n=0
for p in "$std"/std-*; do
    [ -f "$p/avra.toml" ] || continue
    if [ -n "$named" ]; then
        case " $named " in *" $(basename "$p") "*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    else
        case "$COMPILERS" in *" $(basename "$p") "*) continue ;; esac
    fi
    AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$scratch" AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR="$out" AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 "$avra" check "$p" >/dev/null 2>"$scratch/said" ||
        { echo "std_answers: $(basename "$p") is refused by its own compiler:" >&2; cat "$scratch/said" >&2; exit 1; }
    find "$p" -name .avra-cache -type d -prune -exec find {} -delete \;
    n=$((n + 1))

I've measured where the shipped std answers' bytes go, and I'm waiting on the lead's choice of what to cut before changing anything.

**Size after leaving out the compiler's own packages:** 626 MB, down from 1.09 GB. That covers 41 packages and 137 kinds of saved answer ("families").

**Where the bytes go:**
- **Dependency records, not answers, are most of it.** 436 MB is the list of reads each saved answer depends on; the answers themselves are 154 MB.
- **The per-item checks are the biggest single cost.** 21 per-item law-check families save about 18,800 questions each, with empty answers but 214 MB of records.
- **The rest:**
  - tapes and items: 119 MB
  - names, scopes and typing: 107 MB
  - generation and lowering: 45 MB
  - everything else: 103 MB

**What a downstream program reads:** I traced a cold `build` and a cold `check` of a program using `@std.json`. Each reads only its own closure: 319 of the 18,832 std items, about 2%.
- Checking a saved answer means checking every read under it, so anything inside an imported closure gets read. Savings have to come from whole families, not from individual items.
- A downstream `check` also runs the rule and law checks over its dependencies' files, as the old check did. So only 18 families (18 MB) are never asked for. I first told the lead 90 MB from the build trace alone, then corrected it.

**Options to get under 100 MB**, all sent to the lead:
- **(a) Drop the never-asked families:** −18 MB.
- **(b) Merge the 21 per-item law families into one per-item query:** about −200 MB, and it shrinks every user's own store too.
- **(c) Store each read as an index into a per-pack table of hashes**, instead of repeating 16-byte hashes. xz compresses a pack 6.3× and gzip 3.1×, which shows how much repetition there is. This is a store format change and the biggest general win.
- **(d) Ship the answers gzip-compressed and unpack at first use:** shrinks the download only, not the space used on the user's disk.

I recommended (b) then (c), each re-measured to keep the same cold-build times.

**Committed, no cuts:**
- **80666390:** std answers leave out std-avrac, std-http-fuzz, std-http-soak and std-ui_gallery. It also adds `avra cache families [<store>]` (bytes per family) and `AVRA_QUERY_FAMILIES=1` (every family a run asked for).
- **4c9e6447:** `check` reports its families the same way `build` does.

I haven't run the gate on these two commits, and the bundle in `/work` still ends at 2e56e49f.

1. a rule warning (loops.push_loop): shown, exit 0, both paths;

The cost is real for std: a program that only does `use @std.http.{Request}` gets 4 warnings about std-http's and std-http_message's own code (type.alias_copy ×2, lists.bool_comprehension_range, type.coalesce_never; the old path says 3). - (ii) WARNINGS, rule findings and stale citations in a dependency: the user can't act on them in std. For a path dependency, `avra check <dep>` is where they belong. Rust does this (`--cap-lints` for dependencies).

Proposal for the cut:
- A. A check judges warnings, rules and stale citations of the CHECKED package only. That removes the rule families (file_rule_rows, item_fact_found, item_syntax_found, item_alone …), stale_citations and the warning laws from a downstream check, and from what ships. It is a behaviour change on BOTH paths, so the warnings witness's dependency cases flip and the old path gets the same scope.
- B. A dependency's refusals are judged for path dependencies. I answered the lead's question (0) and stopped there: the cut it leads to changes what users see, so I've asked before building it.

**Answer to (0):** a dependency's findings do reach a downstream `check`'s output, verdict and exit code, on both the old path and the program layer. I checked an app that depends on a path dependency, adding four kinds of finding to the dependency one at a time:

| Finding in the dependency | What the app's `check` does (both paths) |
|---|---|
| rule warning (`loops.push_loop`) | shows it, exit 0 |
| law warning (`type.coalesce_never`) | shows it, exit 0 |
| stale `// LICENSED` id | refuses, exit 1 |
| law error (`type.mismatch`) | refuses, exit 1 |

This hurts users of std. A program whose only line is `use @std.http.{Request}` gets 4 warnings about std-http's and std-http_message's own code (the old path shows 3), and the user can't fix any of them.

**What the user actually needs:**
- **Errors in a path dependency:** yes. That's the user's own code, and a build over it fails anyway, so `check` should say why.
- **Errors in the toolchain's std:** these can't happen unless someone edits std. Install already refuses a std that doesn't check clean.
- **Warnings, rule findings and stale citations in any dependency:** no. They belong to `avra check <dependency>`. Rust does the same with `--cap-lints` for dependencies.

**Proposed cut:**
- **A.** A check reports warnings, rule findings and stale citations for the checked package only. That removes the rule families, the warning laws and the stale-citation query from a downstream check, and from what ships. It changes what users see on both paths, so the warnings witness's dependency cases will flip.
- **B.** Errors are still judged for path dependencies. For an unedited toolchain std, the install's clean verdict stands in, checked against the std files' digests, so it gets no law asks at all. An edited std package is judged like a path dependency. This drops the 21 per-item law families from what ships.

After each step I'll measure the cold check time and the shipped size. Then comes (c): storing each read as an index into a per-pack table, not as repeated hashes.

**Waiting on:** the lead's OK to do A, then B.

/// Where the toolchain keeps its verdict on its std, for the binary printed `print`.
fn verdict_at(dir: string, print: string) -> string { joined_path(dir, "verdict-${print}") }

/// The std files of the program on `disk` the toolchain's verdict vouches for, each as `spelled_file`
/// names it: those standing on the toolchain's std, unpinned, whose text is the text it judged.
fn vouched_files(engine: QueryEngine, disk: Disk) -> List<string> {
    let shipped? = shipped_answers() else { return [] }
    let print? = own_print() else { return [] }
    let verdict = read_text(verdict_at(shipped, print)) catch ""
    [spelled_file(f!) for line in verdict.split("\\n") for f in [vouched_line(engine, disk, line)] if f != null]
}

/// The file a verdict's line names, where it stands on the toolchain's std as the verdict judged it.
fn vouched_line(engine: QueryEngine, disk: Disk, line: string) -> SourceFileAddress? {
    let parts = line.split("\\t")
    if parts.length != 3 || !parts[0].starts_with("@std/") || disk.deps.has(parts[0]) { return null }
    let file = SourceFileAddress { package_name: parts[0], path_in_package: parts[1] }

}

/// THE INSTALL'S VERDICT, written where `AVRA_VERDICT_DIR` asks: each of `own`, the files of a std

fn verdict_kept(engine: QueryEngine, own: List<ProgramFile>) {
    // LICENSED input.debug_flag: where an install keeps its verdict is the install's, never an input of what is found
    let dir? = env("AVRA_VERDICT_DIR") else { return }
    let print? = own_print() else { return }
    let lines = [line! for h in own for line in [verdict_line(engine, h.file)] if line != null]
    let _ = append_bytes(verdict_at(dir, print), lines.join("").bytes())
}

/// The verdict's line for `file`: its package, its path, its text's digest.
fn verdict_line(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> string? {
    let text? = source_text(engine, file) else { return null }
    "${file.package_name}\\t${file.path_in_package}\\t${digest_of(text)}\\n"
}

```
/// Every impl, written and generated, the package `package` holds, filed: whether it holds any.
fn impls_filed_in(engine: QueryEngine, package: string) -> bool {
    let written = package_impls(engine, package)
    let generated = package_generated_impls(engine, package)
    !written.parts.is_empty() || !generated.parts.is_empty()
}

/// `files`, the longest first, so processes taking turns share the work about evenly: a file's
/// length is read off its text, which costs nothing a build has not already read.
fn widest_first(engine: QueryEngine, files: List<SourceFileAddress>) -> List<SourceFileAddress> {
    let widths = [source_text(engine, f)?.length ?? 0 for f in files]
    [files[at] for at in sorted_by([at for at in 0..files.length], (a, b) -> widths[a] > widths[b])]
}

/// Where the asking process's time went, phase by phase, and how many packages hold impls.
fn phases_said(clock: QueryTimes, filed: int) -> string { "ahead phases: ${clock.spoken(10)}; impls filed in ${filed} packages" }

#!/bin/sh
# A BINARY IS A FUNCTION OF ITS PACKAGE, NOT OF WHERE THE TREE STANDS. One
# package, a generic instantiated twice, built at two depths: no symbol may
# carry the building machine's path, so the two binaries are the same bytes.
set -u
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/attack.sh"
R=build/moved-tree-attack
rm -rf "$R" && mkdir -p $R/one $R/two/deeper
for d in $R/one/app $R/two/deeper/app; do
    mkdir -p $d/src/a
    printf '[package]\nname = "moved-tree-attack"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n' > $d/avra.toml
    printf 'export fn id<T>(x: T) -> T { x }\n' > $d/src/a/k.av
    printf 'use a.{id}\n\nprintln("${id(3)} ${id("s")}")\n' > $d/src/main.av
    ./avra build $d > $R/out 2> $R/err || { fail "$d did not build: $(head -2 $R/err | tr '\n' ' ')"; continue; }
    got=$($d/src/main 2>&1)
    [ "$got" = "3 s" ] || fail "$d printed '$got', wanted '3 s'"
    cp $d/src/main $d.bin
    # a signature is made where the binary was signed; the code it signs is what is compared
    command -v codesign > /dev/null && codesign --remove-signature $d.bin
done
if [ $fails -eq 0 ]; then
    n=$(cmp -l $R/one/app.bin $R/two/deeper/app.bin 2>&1 | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [ "$n" = 0 ] || fail "the binaries built at two depths differ in $n byte(s)"
fi
verdict "moved-tree-attack" "one package built at two depths"

--- content ---
#!/bin/sh
# AN ANSWER IS THE SAME BYTES IN ANY TREE. A package whose generator writes the place a field was
# written in into the code it generates is built cold in one directory; then, its own store and the
# machine's carried with it, in another, deeper one; then cold there. A stored answer holding the
# first directory's path would build a second binary naming it: the three binaries are the same
# bytes, and each says the place as the package spells it.
set -u
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/attack.sh"
A=${CARRIED_ATTACK_AVRA:-$(pwd)/avra}
R=build/carried-store-attack
find "$R" -delete 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p "$R/one" "$R/two/deeper"
unset AVRA_CACHE_DIR
app="$R/one/app"
mkdir -p "$app/src/gen"
printf '[package]\nname = "carried-store-attack"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n' > "$app/avra.toml"
cat > "$app/src/gen/gen.av" <<'AV'
use @std.meta.{Declared, Type, beside, literal}

/// `@placed`: the type says where its first field was written.
export fn placed(t: Type) -> Declared {
    let file = t.fields.first()?.at?.file ?? "nowhere"
    Declared { made: [beside(t, quote { impl ${t} { static fn written_in() -> string { ${literal(file)} } } })] }
}
AV
printf 'use gen.{placed}\n\n@placed\ntype P = { x: int }\n\nprintln(P.written_in())\n' > "$app/src/main.av"

# `built <dir> <machine cache> <name>`: the package at <dir> built over <machine cache>, its binary kept
built() {
    AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$2" "$A" build "$1" > "$R/$3.out" 2> "$R/$3.err" ||
        { fail "$3 did not build: $(head -3 "$R/$3.err" | tr '\n' ' ')"; return; }
    said=$("$1/src/main" 2>&1)
    [ "$said" = "carried-store-attack/src/main.av" ] || fail "$3 says its place as '$said'"
    cp "$1/src/main" "$R/$3.bin"
    command -v codesign > /dev/null && codesign --remove-signature "$R/$3.bin"
    :
}

built "$app" "$R/machine-one" first
# the package and both stores carried to another directory, deeper
cp -R "$app" "$R/two/deeper/app"
cp -R "$R/machine-one" "$R/machine-carried"
find "$R/two/deeper/app/src" -maxdepth 1 -name main -delete
built "$R/two/deeper/app" "$R/machine-carried" carried
find "$R/two/deeper/app" -name .avra-cache -type d -prune -exec find {} -delete \;
find "$R/two/deeper/app/src" -maxdepth 1 -name main -delete
built "$R/two/deeper/app" "$R/machine-cold" cold
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
    for b in first carried; do
        n=$(cmp -l "$R/$b.bin" "$R/cold.bin" 2>&1 | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
        [ "$n" = 0 ] || fail "the $b binary and the cold one differ in $n byte(s): $(strings -n 8 "$R/$b.bin" | grep -F "$PWD/$R" | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
    done
fi
verdict "carried-store-attack" "one package built in two trees, its stores carried, against cold"

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK: the old path's check the net runs first is not that work.
AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
    "$builder" build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {

// ── Strings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Value equality; null equals only null.
// TEXT IS A LENGTH AND BYTES, NEVER A TERMINATOR. A NUL is a
// character like any other — `from_codepoint(0)` mints one with no
// foreign input at all — so a comparison that stops at the first one
// answers about a PREFIX and calls it the whole string. `"ab\0cd"`
// read EQUAL to `"ab"` while `.length` said 5. The length comes
// first: unequal lengths are unequal text in O(1), where `strcmp`
// scanned to the first difference.
int64_t avra_streq(const char* a, const char* b) {
    CENSUS(g_streqs++);
    // one box is one text: a literal compared at its own call site is
    // the same static box every time
    if (a == b) return 1;
    if (a == NULL || b == NULL) return 0;

    -exec cp {} "$src/build/" \;
printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" > "$out/snapshot"
cache=$root/$out/cache

# One run of the census compiler in the snapshot, once what it reads is older than the stamp window:
# its census to <name>.out, what it printed to <name>.stdout.
counted() {
    name=$1; shift
    sleep 3
    started=$(date +%s)
    # the census reports at exit only where the run accounts (AVRA_MEM_STATS)
    (cd "$src" && AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \
        sh "$root/tools/memcap.sh" "${COST_CAP_MB:-8000}" taskset -c 0 build/avra "$@" \
        > "$root/$out/$name.stdout" 2> "$root/$out/$name.out") || {
        tail -20 "$out/$name.out"; echo "cost: $name failed ($*)"; exit 1; }
    echo "cost: $name $(($(date +%s) - started)) s"
}

# One warm findings run of the cli, its `worked:` line kept as <name>.out, its census beside it.

/// A package's own store, and the shared store beneath it, with where each package's sources
/// stand. The shared store answers for the compiler binary printed `shared_print`, whatever queries
/// a command asks of it.
export type LayeredStore = { own: DiskStore, shared: DiskStore?, places: List<PackagePlace>, shared_print: string }

//! SETS OF NAMES, EACH KEPT ONCE: a set is an id, the same id for the same members whatever order
//! they came in, so a question's set is one number and the union of two sets is looked up once. Id
//! zero is the empty set. An identity: every holder sees one table.
use @std.meta.{identity}
use sorted.{sorted_by}
use @std.text.{text_before}

@identity
export type NameSets = {
    /// Each set's members, sorted, by its id.
    members: Cell<List<List<string>>>,
    /// Each set's id, by its members spelled.
    ids: Cell<Map<string, int>>,
    /// Each union asked, by the two ids.
    unions: Cell<Map<string, int>>,
}

/// A table holding only the empty set.
export fn name_sets() -> NameSets {

The machine store's layering is cheap now, committed as 33b1ae92 on `avra-lane-defects` for batch 58. On check-program it costs about 15.6K extra string compares instead of 518K.

**Cause:** with the machine store on, the engine tracks which packages every answer reads, to decide which store keeps it. Three lookups in that bookkeeping compared strings every time:
- Combining two packages' read sets was looked up under the text of their two ids (`"a,b"`).
- Whether a set is shared was looked up under `"${id}"`.
- Finding a path's package scanned all ~45 package places, comparing strings each time.

**Fix:**
- The combined sets and the shared flags now sit in std-program's integer-keyed table (`HashKeyedTable`), keyed by the ids themselves. Avra's `Map` only takes text keys, so it couldn't do this.
- Package places are now two lookup tables: root to package, and package to whether the machine store serves it. A path's package is found by walking up its directories to the nearest root.

**Census string compares**, cold over the base55 snapshot:

| Workload | Before | After | Pre-4d873bb0 level |
|---|---|---|---|
| check-program, machine store on | 45,297,487 | 44,673,659 | 44,992,531 |
| check-program, machine store off | — | 44,658,049 | |
| check-cli, machine store on | 271,323,071 | 264,785,978 | 274,455,796 |

Both workloads are now below the level from before the licence check.

**Gate:** the program, idioms, witness-b and cli slices pass. The container restarted partway through; witness-b and cli were re-run afterwards and passed.

I also freed about 31 GB of disk (it was down to 10 GB) by deleting only my own measurement caches with `find -delete`.

/// A question: which query, a hash of its code, its arguments as bytes, what it's known by, and
/// whether those bytes spell its arguments' keys rather than save them.
@derive(Saved)
export type Question = { query_name: string, code_hash: string, arguments: Bytes, known_as: ContentHash, keyed: bool = false }

/// A question, with what it's known by across processes. Its code's hash is part of that, so a
/// changed query never finds its old answers. The name and the code are counted, so they can't

        query_name: query_name,
        code_hash: code_hash,
        arguments: arguments,
        known_as: content_hash(counted.concat(arguments)),
    }
}

### 2026-11-20T03:32:51 AGENT
The repetition is large: **2,259,794 whole reads, only 244,728 distinct** (9.2×), and 232,766 part reads with 72,322 distinct (3.2×). The pack is 454 MB now: records 168 MB, answers 269 MB. Posting the design and arithmetic before building, since this changes the shared store's format.

<to_controller>DESIGN (c), dictionary-indexed reads. Measured on the shipped std pack (`avra cache families`'s new reads line): 454 MB = records 168 + answers 269. Reads: 2,259,794 whole, 244,728 distinct (9.2× repeat); 232,766 part, 72,322 distinct (3.2×).
1. Keyed by: each pack gets a READ TABLE, the distinct (question, whole answer seen) pairs and the distinct part reads, sorted by hash and written in the pack's index. A record holds a read as its table index (a varint, ~3 B) instead of 32 B (whole) or 64 B (part). Records are still checked where they lie: an index resolves through the pack's table.
2. Also: a QUESTION TABLE of (query_name, code_hash) per pack. Each question now spells both as text; a few hundred distinct against ~300K questions.
3. Drafts: a segment interns its reads as it streams records, and the table is written at seal. ABSORB AND COMPACTION CAN'T COPY A RECORD'S OCTETS ANY MORE, since indices are per pack: a carried record is re-encoded against the new pack's table (one table lookup per read). That is the real cost of (c). Absorb gets slower in proportion to reads carried; I'd measure it on the warm-edit receipt.
4. Format: a new pack format (QUESTION_SHAPE / pack-format bump), so an old store reads as cold, never wrong.
5. Arithmetic: whole reads 72 MB → ~15 MB (dictionary 7.8 + indices ~7); part reads 15 → ~5 MB; question names/code hashes ~30 → ~1 MB. Records 168 → ~65 MB, pack 454 → ~350 MB.
**So (c) alone doesn't reach < 100 MB.** The rest is answers: lowering every std body is ~180 MB (lowered_under 51, lowered_method_under 40, body_facts 49, method_body_typed 23 of answers). Options:
- (e) ship no lowering: a dependent lowers the bodies it reaches. I can measure the cold cost first; for json the build reaches ~200 bodies;
- (d) gzip the shipped pack, ÷3.
(c)+(e) is likely ~100 MB.
Recommendation: measure (e) first (cheap: a dependents' pass without bodies_lowered, then re-time cold json and http builds). Then (c), which shrinks every store and not only the shipped one. Your call on order, and on whether (c)'s absorb cost is acceptable.</to_controller>

I've measured and written up (c), and I'm waiting for the lead's call before changing the store format.

**Measured on the shipped std pack (454 MB):** records are 168 MB and answers 269 MB.

| | Total | Distinct | Repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whole reads | 2,259,794 | 244,728 | 9.2× |
| Part reads | 232,766 | 72,322 | 3.2× |

**The design I posted:**
- **Read table:** each pack keeps one table of its distinct reads, and a record stores each read as a small index into it instead of 32 or 64 bytes of hashes.
- **Question table:** the same for each question's query name and code hash.
- **The real cost:** when packs are merged or compacted, records can no longer be copied as raw bytes, because the indices belong to one pack. Each record would have to be re-encoded against the new pack's table, so merging gets slower in proportion to the reads it carries.
- **Old stores:** the format version changes, so an old store reads as cold, never wrong.

**Estimate:** records drop from 168 MB to about 65 MB, so the pack goes from 454 MB to about 350 MB. That isn't enough on its own for the 100 MB target.

Most of what's left is answers. Lowering every std body accounts for about 180 MB of them. I proposed two ways to deal with that:
- **(e)** stop shipping lowering, so a program lowers only the std bodies it actually reaches.
- **(d)** gzip the shipped pack, which shrinks the download about 3×.

My recommendation is to measure (e) first, since it's cheap to test, then build (c), which shrinks every store, not just the shipped one.

One more thing: `avra cache families` now prints a line counting total and distinct reads. It builds and is used for these numbers, but it isn't committed yet.

Then (c), on one condition: the owner's rule is never to trade warm for cold, so (c) lands only if the warm one-edit rows (cost gate edit-*, plus a warm `build packages/cli` wall) don't rise. If absorb's re-encode shows there, give the warm path a pack-local table (copy the octets when source and destination share a table) and measure again. (d) only if both fall short.

The honest way is a new pass that lowers, per package, only what other std packages ask of it.

### 2026-11-20T03:51:08 AGENT
Reading the code changes the scope of (c). A record's bytes are self-contained today, and they travel:
- copied as raw octets into a merged pack (`carried`);
- shared between forked work-ahead processes (the wave table, `wave_kept`);
- adopted from the wave into a process's own store;
- held unsaved in `held_questions`.

Indexing reads into a per-pack table makes a record unreadable without its table at every one of those hops. Telling the lead before going further.

<to_controller>(c) SCOPING, before I cut: dictionary-indexed reads is much bigger than the pack writer. Today a record's bytes are SELF-CONTAINED and travel four ways:
1. raw octets into a merged pack (`carried`);
2. into the wave table the forked work-ahead processes share (`wave_kept`/`wave_records`);
3. adopted from the wave into a process's own store (`adopted`);
4. held unsaved (`held_questions`), and read in place everywhere (`RecordWords.Laid`).
With indices into a per-pack table, a record can't be read without its table at each hop, so the wave needs a shared table, adoption re-encodes, compaction re-encodes, and the warm path's absorb re-encodes. Your fallback (copy octets when source and destination share a table) only helps if tables are append-only across generations.
Honest estimate: several days, touching the store every lane depends on, with the warm path at real risk.
Alternatives on the table:
- (d) compressing the SHIPPED pack only is isolated (std_answers.sh plus lay-in). std-compress has gzip, zlib and brotli: gzip measured 3.1× on a pack, so full 454 → ~146 MB shipped; brotli is likely ~4× → ~110 MB. The machine store stays 454 MB on disk.
- (c-lite), self-contained: intern each question's (query_name, code_hash) text per pack. It's ~30 MB of records, every question carries both as text, and it needs no hop to change (the Question is decoded once at read).
The warm-row baseline is running now regardless (base57 snapshot: the cost gate's edit-* rows and a warm `build packages/cli` wall). Which do you want: (c) in full (I'll plan it as its own multi-step item), or (d) first plus (c-lite)?</to_controller>

type Packing = { suffix: string, format: Format }

/// The ways a pack ships packed.
const PACKINGS: List<Packing> = [Packing { suffix: ".br", format: Format.Brotli }, Packing { suffix: ".gz", format: Format.Gzip }]

/// The most octets a shipped pack unpacks to.
const UNPACKED_MOST: int = 17179869184

/// The pack shipped at `from` laid at `to`, unpacked where it was packed, unless one stands there;
/// why it couldn't be, otherwise.
fn pack_laid(from: string, to: string) -> Result<string, string> {
    if exists(to) { return .Ok(to) }
    let octets = match read_bytes(from) { .Ok(b) -> b, .Err(e) -> { return .Err(e.describe().message) } }
    let packing = packed_as(from)
    let unpacked = if packing == null { octets } else {
        match decoded(octets, packing!.format, UNPACKED_MOST) { .Ok(b) -> b, .Err(_) -> { return .Err(unpacking_failed(from)) } }
    }
    match file_laid(to, unpacked) { .Ok(at) -> .Ok(at), .Err(e) -> .Err(e.describe().message) }
}

/// `avra cache shipped <dir> [brotli|gzip]`: EVERY PACK IN `dir` PACKED FOR SHIPPING, each beside
/// itself under its packing's suffix and the pack itself let go, so a toolchain ships its answers
/// small and a lay-in unpacks them. Says what the packs weighed and weigh now.
fn shipped_packed(dir: string, spelled: string) -> int {
    let packing? = PACKINGS.find(it.format == packing_named(spelled)) else { return 2 }
    mut before = 0
    mut after = 0
    for name in list_dir(dir) catch [] {
        if packed_as(name) != null || !name.starts_with("pack-") { continue }
        let at = joined_path(dir, name)
        let octets = match read_bytes(at) { .Ok(b) -> b, .Err(e) -> { eprintln("avra cache shipped: ${e.describe().message}"); return 1 } }
        let packed = match encoded(octets, packing.format, null) { .Ok(b) -> b, .Err(_) -> { eprintln(unpacking_failed(at)); return 1 } }
        match file_laid(at + packing.suffix, packed) { .Ok(_) -> {}, .Err(e) -> { eprintln("avra cache shipped: ${e.describe().message}"); return 1 } }
        let _ = remove(at)
        before = before + octets.length
        after = after + packed.length
    }
    println("avra cache shipped: ${before / 1024} KB packed to ${after / 1024} KB as ${packing.suffix}")
    0
}

/// The packing a word names: brotli, else gzip for `gzip`.
fn packing_named(spelled: string) -> Format { if spelled == "gzip" { Format.Gzip } else { Format.Brotli } }

fn unpacking_failed(path: string) -> string { "${path} does not pack or unpack as its suffix says" }

'''

Packs are never rewritten in place, and merging writes new files and removes old ones, so a link is safe. std-io has no hard-link function yet, so this needs a small runtime addition.

#!/bin/sh
# THE TOOLCHAIN'S STD ANSWERS SERVE A PROGRAM'S FIRST CHECK, AND NEVER WRONGLY. A toolchain is laid
# out as `make install` lays one (bin/avra, lib/avra/std, lib/avra/answers), shipping the answers its
# compiler keeps over @std/text, and a program over @std/text is checked against it:
#   (1) on a fresh machine, the shipped packs are laid in, and the check says what a check with no
#       machine store says, its own store holding less than half of what that one's does;
#   (2) two first checks at once on one fresh machine both say it, and leave every pack whole and
#       no draft behind;
#   (3) a compiler of another print lays nothing in;
#   (4) a machine store that can't stand, or a disk too small for the packs (where this machine can
#       mount one), costs one line on stderr and nothing else: the check says what it says without;
#   (5) the install's verdict stands only for the std it judged: an installed std file edited to a
#       type error is judged again, and the program's check refuses it.
#   sh tools/std_answers_attack.sh [compiler]     (default build/avra-try)

avra=$(cd "$(dirname "${1:-$root/build/avra-try}")" && pwd)/$(basename "${1:-$root/build/avra-try}")
w=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/avra-std-answers.XXXXXX")
mounted=""
trap '[ -n "$mounted" ] && umount "$mounted" 2>/dev/null; find "$w" -delete 2>/dev/null || :' EXIT

export type ContentHash = { high_word: int, low_word: int }

impl ContentHash {
    /// The hash as one text, what a table of what its answer reads back as is keyed by.
    fn held_key() -> string { "${self.high_word}:${self.low_word}" }

    /// An order over hashes, for keeping them sorted.
    fn comes_before(other: ContentHash) -> bool {
        self.high_word < other.high_word ||

    fn same_as(other: ContentHash) -> bool { self.high_word == other.high_word && self.low_word == other.low_word }
}

`known_as` is 128 bits: `content_hash` is BLAKE3 cut to its first 16 octets, as two 64-bit words (`answer_record.av:30` and `:55`, `hash_of_digest` reads the words at offsets 0 and 8). It hashes the shape tag (`saved`/`keyed` plus `QUESTION_SHAPE`), then the query name and code hash, each with a length prefix, then the arguments. That isn't under 128, so under your rule I'll drop the code hash entirely rather than keep an 8-byte prefix. One more point: the store already finds a kept question and its answers by this same 128-bit `known_as`. A collision there would hand back the wrong record before any code-hash compare ran, so the stored code hash never guarded against more than what the lookup key already does. The receipt will state this: "known_as: BLAKE3, first 128 bits, over shape‖name‖code_hash‖arguments; the code hash is left out of the kept question, and a kept question is re-asked only where today's definition rebuilds the same known_as". (c-lite), first receipt: the shrink was smaller than I estimated. **known_as: BLAKE3, first 128 bits, over shape‖name‖code_hash‖arguments**, so the hash is dropped entirely and no prefix is kept. Results: the code-hash spelling appears 0 times in the new packs (it appeared 85,756 times, 6.9 MB of text), unpacked answers go from 444 to 432 MB, and the brotli-packed size goes from 107.6 MB to 104.0 MiB (109.2 MB decimal for the dir). My ~55 MB estimate assumed ~600K stored questions; there are ~86K, and brotli was already folding the repeated decimal text, so this alone doesn't reach 100 MB. `cache families` says where the bytes are: answers are ~330 MB, led by lowered_under, lowered_method_under and body_facts. Records are ~100 MB, carrying 2.3M whole reads, of which only 250K are distinct (32 high-entropy bytes each). Shipping packs at brotli q5 with lgwin 22 (a 4 MB window), so most of those repeats fall outside its window. I'm measuring q5/7/9/11 at lgwin 24 (16 MB, still standard brotli, any decoder) on the big pack, encode and decode times included. If a standard setting gets under 100 MB within the 0.1 s first-use budget, the cheapest landing is a packing knob rather than a format change. If not, the next self-contained shrink is the read lists. The (c-lite) patch is uncommitted until the warm and cold receipts are in.

/// 24, clamped, absent its default 22. A wider one finds repeats
/// further apart, and asks a reader for that much memory; at 24 any
/// brotli decoder still reads it. zlib's window is its own 15 bits.

use @std.meta.{Type, Directive, Code, Kind, name, literal, list_of}
use @std.validate.{Decode, Value, Entry}

export trait Fields {
    static fn derive(t: Type) -> List<Directive> {
        let entries = list_of(
            [quote {
            Entry { key: ${literal(f.name)}, value: ${written(f.kind, name(f.name))} }
        } for f in t.fields],
        )
        Decode.supplied(t, quote { Value.Map(${entries}) })
    }
}

fn written(k: Kind, v: Code) -> Code {
    let text = match k {
        .Str or .Opt(.Str) -> quote { Value.Text(value) },
        rest -> quote { unsupported_test_projection() },
    }
    quote {
        match ${v} {
            value? -> ${text}
            null -> Value.Null
        }
    }
}

**Which store.** `~/.avra/cache` holds three things:
1. `cas/`: the old compiler's shared blobs.
2. `prints/<16 hex of the compiler print>/{store,bin,obj}`: **the old std-avrac compiler's machine-wide row store**.
3. `tapes/`: the program layer's machine store, the only one `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE` governs (`tapes.av:324`, one cell for the whole process).

**What keys it.** A module's record (`Stored.Sig`, `node_key[root, module]` → interface digest → body) holds a file whose text didn't move. #!/bin/sh
# A DERIVE'S NEW MEMBERS ARE SEEN ON THE NEXT CHECK. A package's own trait derives `first` beside a
# type, through `beside(t, quote { impl ${t} { … } })`; a test of that package passes; a second member
# is added inside the quoted impl, and the test calling it is run again over the same machine cache:
#   (1) the program layer alone (AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0) sees `second`;
#   (2) the default path (the program layer, the old path judging beside it) sees `second`;
#   (3) the old path alone (AVRA_PROGRAM=0) sees `second`.
# (2) and (3) fail while the old store stands: its machine pack (`prints/<print>/store` under the
# machine cache) keeps the deriving module's record, and a member added inside a quoted impl moves
# nothing its runs' reads are judged by. They are the witness the old store's deletion carries: owed
# until then, so this is no gate row. `WITNESS_NET_ONLY=1` holds (1) alone.
#   sh tools/derive_members_witness.sh [compiler]     (default build/avra)
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
avra=$(cd "$(dirname "${1:-$root/build/avra}")" && pwd)/$(basename "${1:-$root/build/avra}")
w=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/avra-derive-members.XXXXXX")
trap 'find "$w" -delete 2>/dev/null || :' EXIT
fail() { echo "derive_members_witness: $*"; exit 1; }
held() { echo "derive_members_witness: $*"; }

laid() {
    p="$w/$1"
    mkdir -p "$p/src/tests"
    cat > "$p/avra.toml" <<'EOF'
[package]
name        = "@probe/drv"
version     = "0.0.1"
description = "a derive whose generated members change"

[lib]
name = "probe-drv"
path = "src/drv.av"
EOF
    cat > "$p/src/made.av" <<'EOF'
use @std.meta.{Type, Directive, beside, literal}

export trait Made {
    static fn derive(t: Type) -> List<Directive> {
        [beside(t, quote {
            impl ${t} {
                static fn first() -> string { ${literal("one")} }
            }
        })]
    }
}
EOF
    cat > "$p/src/drv.av" <<'EOF'
use @std.meta.{derive}
use made.{Made}

@derive(Made)
export type Point = { x: int }
EOF
    cat > "$p/src/tests/drv_test.av" <<'EOF'
use @probe.drv.{Point}

spec "drv" {
    given "a derived member" {
        then "first" { Point.first() == "one" }
    }
}
EOF
}

grown() {
    p="$w/$1"
    sed -i.was 's|                static fn first() -> string { ${literal("one")} }|&\
                static fn second() -> int { 2 }|' "$p/src/made.av"
    sed -i.was 's|        then "first" { Point.first() == "one" }|&\
        then "second" { Point.second() == 2 }|' "$p/src/tests/drv_test.av"
    find "$p" -name '*.was' -delete
}

# one case: a fresh package and machine cache under `$2...` as env, run, grown, run again
seen() {
    name=$1
    shift
    laid "$name"
    mkdir -p "$w/$name-cache"
    env AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$w/$name-cache" "$@" "$avra" test "$w/$name" > "$w/$name.first" 2>&1 ||
        fail "($name) the first member's test failed: $(head -3 "$w/$name.first")"
    grown "$name"
    env AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$w/$name-cache" "$@" "$avra" test "$w/$name" > "$w/$name.grown" 2>&1
}

seen net AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 || fail "(1) the program layer alone missed the new member: $(grep -m1 'error\[' "$w/net.grown")"
held "(1) the program layer alone sees a derive's new member"
[ "${WITNESS_NET_ONLY:-0}" = 1 ] && exit 0
seen default X=1 || fail "(2) the default path missed the new member: $(grep -m1 'error\[' "$w/default.grown")"
held "(2) the default path sees a derive's new member"
seen old AVRA_PROGRAM=0 || fail "(3) the old path missed the new member: $(grep -m1 'error\[' "$w/old.grown")"
held "(3) the old path sees a derive's new member"
echo "derive_members_witness: held"

I'm growing a cache with a default-path cold build of the cli (the path services ran), to see where exit time goes once the store is large.

<to_controller>
fmt spin / exit spin, early findings. **Not reproduced on HEAD with this machine's default cache** (cas 784 MB, prints 1.3 GB, tapes 1.9 GB): `fmt --check` on relation.av takes 332 ms cold and 29 ms warm; no std-relation file goes over 350 ms; `test std-text` and `check std-relation` exit 0.01–0.03 s after their last output, and no process is left behind. The machine store isn't in base57, so on the batch-57 Mac a large `~/.avra/cache` means the **old store** (`cas/` plus `prints/<print>/store`). Its exit work, `settle` → `pack_settle`, has three whole-store walks:
1. `seal` runs **`sealed_whole` (materializes every record)** whenever any key is withdrawn (`any_withdrawn`) or runs reach `RUNS_KEPT`, so a run that invalidates one row pays for every row the store holds;
2. `enforce_limits` → `prune_bodies` reads chains, and `trim_kept_files` lists and stats every kept obj and bin;
3. `cas_fitted` lists and stats every blob, then sorts them, whenever the run put one.

I'm now growing a store with a cold cli build in a fresh cache, then timing an edit's exit under `AVRA_QTRACE` (`Q store sealed … took`), to see which of these carries the ~90 s. The fix will make exit work scale with what the run wrote: a withdrawal recorded in a run (as a tombstone) instead of forcing a whole fold, and trims that walk only when what the run added crosses a ceiling. Note that this is std-avrac's old store, which the flip deletes. If the measurement puts the time there, I'll ask before changing it: is it worth fixing for batch 58/59, given it dies with the old path?

--- content ---
#!/bin/sh
# WITH THE NET OFF, NOTHING WRITES THE OLD STORE. The old compiler's store keeps its rows in the
# machine cache (`cas/`, `prints/<print>/`) and its checkout's history in the tree's `.avra-cache`;
# its exit work (a whole fold, the trims) walks what it holds, so a large one spins after a run. A
# fresh package over a fresh machine cache, with AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0, is checked cold, edited,
# checked, tested and built:
#   (1) the machine cache holds no file under `cas/` or `prints/`;
#   (2) the tree's `.avra-cache` holds nothing but the program layer's (`tapes*`);
#   (0) and, so (1) can see a write at all, the same runs with the net on do write `prints/`.
# (0) goes with the old path; (1) and (2) are what the flip leaves.
#   sh tools/net_off_old_store_witness.sh [compiler]     (default build/avra)
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
avra=$(cd "$(dirname "${1:-$root/build/avra}")" && pwd)/$(basename "${1:-$root/build/avra}")
w=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/avra-net-off-store.XXXXXX")
trap 'find "$w" -delete 2>/dev/null || :' EXIT
fail() { echo "net_off_old_store_witness: $*"; exit 1; }
held() { echo "net_off_old_store_witness: $*"; }

laid() {
    p="$w/$1"
    mkdir -p "$p/src/tests"
    cat > "$p/avra.toml" <<'EOF'
[package]
name        = "@probe/oldstore"
version     = "0.0.1"
description = "a package checked, edited, tested and built"

[bin]
name = "probe-oldstore"
path = "src/main.av"
EOF
    cat > "$p/src/made.av" <<'EOF'
export fn said() -> string { "one" }
EOF
    cat > "$p/src/main.av" <<'EOF'
use made.{said}

fn main() { println(said()) }
EOF
    cat > "$p/src/tests/made_test.av" <<'EOF'
use made.{said}

spec "made" {
    given "a word" {
        then "said" { said().length == 3 }
    }
}
EOF
}

# the runs under `$2...` as env, over the package `$1` and a machine cache of its own
ran() {
    name=$1
    shift
    laid "$name"
    c="$w/$name-cache"

<to_controller>
DERIVE COST, first measurements. **The derive's cost is linear, and the bytes are the evaluator never freeing, not the derive keeping its code.** Synthetic `@derive(Saved)` enums (a quarter of variants bare, the rest with 1–3 fields), settle lines under `AVRA_DEBUG=1`, net off, cold:

| variants | steps | peak bytes |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 46,029 | 0.78 MB |
| 32 | 91,397 | 1.50 MB |
| 64 | 182,133 | 2.96 MB |
| 128 | 363,605 | 5.87 MB |

That's ~45 KB per variant held, against ~675 bytes per variant of generated source (`avra expand`), **67× the output**.

Where it goes, from probes on a tiny derive:
- The `Type` input *alone* costs ~1.6 KB per bare variant, and holds no code at all.
- One quoted arm `.${v} -> ${n}` costs ~2.2 KB on top of a bare `Node.Int` code (~0.7 KB).
- The quote's literal text costs nothing: `parts` are shared constant strings, and a 60-byte-longer arm measured byte-identical.

The cause: `budgeted_machine` (every settlement, a generator's included, `interp.av:693`) runs with **`freeing: false`**. Nothing a derive allocates is ever freed, so "peak" is the **sum of every box it ever made**, garbage included: each quote's fresh `parts` list, its fills list, its node, its `Arms`/`Code` wrapper, every comprehension's list. Second effect: with freeing off, `shared()` is true for every box, so **every in-place write copies first**. The comment says why it's off: "its values cross into and out of `MetaVal` heaps whose references the memory pass never saw".

Now: a measurement-only switch (`AVRA_SETTLE_FREEING=1`, never committed) is rebuilding. With it I'll measure (a) the curve with freeing on, (b) whether every std derive's expansion stays byte-identical with it on (a wrong count would trap as "a freed box was reached", or worse, silently reuse a spare id), and (c) real Seating before and after. Then I'll propose one of:
1. free in settlement runs, made safe: counts held right where values cross in and out of `MetaVal`, perhaps without reusing a freed id so a bad count always traps;
2. if that's too wide, cut what the derive and the quote lowering allocate per variant: a static `parts` list per quote site, fewer wrapper boxes. That shrinks the constant, but it stays allocation-bound.
</to_controller>

use @std.meta.{Type, Directive, Code, Arms, beside, name}

type Folds = { own: fn(Code) -> Code, held: fn(Code, Code) -> Code }

fn leaf_folds(leaf: fn(Code) -> Code) -> Folds {
    Folds { own: leaf, held: (e: Code, _cell: Code) -> leaf(e) }
}

fn identity_of(e: Code) -> Code { quote { ${e}.length } }

fn arm(v: string, f: Folds) -> Arms { quote { .${name(v)} -> ${f.held(name("x"), name("y"))} } }

export trait Gen {
    static fn derive(t: Type) -> List<Directive> {
        let f = leaf_folds(identity_of)
        let arms: List<Arms> = [arm(v.name, f) for v in t.variants]
        [beside(t, quote {
            impl ${t} {
                fn number(x: string) -> int { match self { ${arms} } }
            }
        })]
    }
}

// A spread copies a list's records into a new list, and the list it read is let go at once: each
// copied record is the new list's to hold. Handed through a fn that answers its own argument, the
// copy is read after its source is gone — the evaluator once let the source's release free them.
type Stmt = { node: string }

fn passed(statements: List<Stmt>) -> List<Stmt> {
    if statements.is_empty() { [Stmt { node: "none" }] } else { statements }
}

fn made(n: int) -> List<Stmt> { [Stmt { node: "a${k}" } for k in 0..n] }

fn spread(lead: bool, n: int) -> List<Stmt> {
    let first: List<Stmt> = if lead { [Stmt { node: "c" }] } else { [] }
    passed([..first, ..made(n)])
}

fn nodes(xs: List<Stmt>) -> string { [x.node for x in xs].join(",") }

<to_controller>
DERIVE COST, **the trap's cause is found, and it's a live bug today.** Minimised to 15 lines: a spread `[..first, ..made(n)]` lowers to `extend(r11, r4); release r4; extend(r11, r5); release r5`. The **evaluator's `extended` copies the source's slots without taking their references** (`interp.av`, `self.arrays[d].concat(self.arrays[s])`). The C runtime's `array_append` copies an owned slot through `avra_array_push_owned`, which retains ("RETAIN-AT-PACK"). So in the evaluator, `release r5` frees records the new list still holds.

It's live in ordinary programs: a plain package with that shape (records spread into a list, handed through a fn answering its argument) gives:

| | result |
|---|---|
| layer `run --eval` | **defect: a freed box was reached** |
| old `run --eval` | **defect** |
| old native | **defect** |
| layer native | `c,a0,a1,a2` (correct) |

Never-freeing settlement runs hid it in derives. All 32 traps over std-avrac (`Taped`'s `variant_written`/`untaped_chosen`/`variant_read`, `copied_derive`, `tape_schema`) were freed at a release just after a spread, then read in `@std/meta`'s `stmts_nodes`.

Fix, at the cause: `extended` retains each copied element, as `push_owned` does in C, and refuses a freed source. I checked the evaluator's other element-copying rows against their C twins: `concat` already retains through `shared_array`, and `array_filled` (an unmarked fill) and `EnumBoxed` (a moved payload) match their C twins. Regression: a new program test, `features/lists/tests/spread_owned` (eval == native == expected).

/// WHETHER A FILE STANDS CANONICAL: its text printed back is its text, byte for byte. The answer is
/// kept with what it read — the file's text and its words' shapes — so a file nobody edited, under
/// providers nobody edited, is not parsed or printed again.
@query
export fn file_canonical(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress) -> Canonical {
    match file_formatted(engine, file) {
        .Ok(text) -> if "${text}\n" == source_text(engine, file) ?? "" { Canonical.Stands } else { Canonical.Differs },
        .Err(report) -> Canonical.Refused(report.split("\n").first() ?? report),
    }
}

extern fn avra_cpu_ns() -> int

/// Burns `ms` milliseconds of CPU, then answers `word`.
fn burned(ms: int, word: string) -> Bytes {
    let until = avra_cpu_ns() + ms * 1000000
    mut turns = 0
    while avra_cpu_ns() < until { turns = turns + 1 }
    word.bytes()

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS BUILD: exact retain/release/list-write counts, and the
# callers that cause them. Counting costs ~8% of a run, so it never
# ships: a census compiler is built BESIDE build/avra, from a runtime
# compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, and the shipping runtime library is
# rebuilt on every exit.
#   sh tools/census.sh check packages/std-avrac
#
# THE SHIPPING COMPILER IS NEVER REMOVED. It builds the census
# compiler, so a census that deletes it first has nothing to build
# with, and every recovery that rebuilds needs the memory and disk the
# census run just spent.
#
# CENSUS_EDIT MEASURES A WARM EDIT: the command runs once cold to fill the store,
# then CENSUS_EDIT edits the tree, and only the run after it is counted.
#   CENSUS_EDIT='sh tools/db_measure/edit_literal.sh' sh tools/census.sh check packages/cli
#
# A CENSUS THAT PRINTS NO COUNTS FAILS. A check that examined nothing
# is not a check that passed: no `rc:` line means the binary carried no
# census, and the run exits 1 saying so.
# A cold run clears the tree's `.avra-cache`; the machine store lives there too, or "cold" would read the machine's rows.
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK, under a memory cap: the old path's check the net runs
# before the program layer's is not that work, and its memory with the layer's passes the cap.

- **One reader:** `@std.program.query_times.query_times_asked()` is a `once` read of `AVRA_QUERY_TIMES=1`, and it's the only read of the flag in the tree. The cli's ten `env("AVRA_QUERY_TIMES")` reads are gone (tapes, check_program, lowered), along with `item_ahead`'s own `timed_ahead()` and the separate `AVRA_QUERY_FAMILIES` dump.
- **One clock:** asked for its times, a process times every engine it makes into one process-wide `QueryTimes` (`process_times()`). That includes the engines a build makes after each merge, and work-ahead's phase clock, so its "files parsed"/"generators run" rows land there too. Unasked, `time_queries()` (the `--time` flags) keeps a fresh clock per engine, as before.
- **One table:** `QueryTimes.family_table()` has columns `family calls computed reused folded cpu_s wall_s` (pinned as `FAMILY_COLUMNS`). A query's computed/reused/folded sides make one row; phases outside the engine (a build's merges, the answers taken, the store saved) are rows of their own, which is where wall per wave shows. Rows run by CPU, most first.
- **One exit:** `main.av`'s single `exit` goes through `times_ended(code)`, which prints `families:` plus the table once, for whatever command ran.

`times_said` keeps only its phases/split/cutoff lines.

//! A METHOD CHAIN FOLDED INTO ONE PIPELINE — `xs.filter(p).map(f)` is
//! one loop and no intermediate list. Typing recorded each adapter's
//! stage (`PipeStage`); lowering walks the chain from its base outward,
//! lowering the base source FIRST and boxing each fn once in source
//! order, then runs the whole chain into a push. A subject that is no
//! adapter (a `concat`, a plain list) is the head the rest folds over.
use core.{ExprId, Reg, TypeId, Type, Arrow}
use features.{LowerCx, MethodCall, PipeStage, FnBox, Step, Clause, Sink, Source, Pipeline}

/// `xs.map(f)` / `xs.filter(p)` — the chain ending here, run once.
export fn chained(mut cx: LowerCx, mc: MethodCall) -> Reg {
    let clauses? = chain_clauses(cx, mc.e) else { return cx.lower_defect(mc.e, "a chain link without its stage survived typing") }
    if cx.seen_at(mc.e) is .Map { return cx.piped(Pipeline { clauses: clauses, sink: .Put(cx.map_new(cx.shape_at(mc.e))) }) }
    let dst = cx.grown_box(cx.shape_at(mc.e), cx.box_size(0), [])
    cx.piped(Pipeline { clauses: clauses, sink: .Push(dst) })
}

/// `xs.find(p)` over a chain — no list, the first hit's cell.
export fn found_chain(mut cx: LowerCx, mc: MethodCall, s: Seat) -> Reg {
    let clauses = subject_clauses(cx, mc.subject)
    let opt = cx.type_at(mc.e)
    let cell = absent_cell(cx, opt)
    cx
        .piped(Pipeline { clauses: clauses, sink: .Find(opt, cell, step_of(cx, s.arg, cx.type(bool))) })
}

/// item one process's alone, answers each it takes that it knows nothing of, publishes, and
/// leaves without tidying up.
fn answered_and_gone<T, R>(
    store: LayeredStore,
    definitions: List<QueryDefinition>,
    items: List<T>,
    is_known: fn(QueryEngine, T) -> bool,
    ask: fn(QueryEngine, T) -> R,
    group: int,
    core: int,
    timed: bool,
    learned_at: string,
) {
    let engine = query_engine(store, definitions)
    if timed { engine.time_queries() }
    mut answered = 0
    mut turn = avra_cores_claimed(group)
    while turn < items.length {
        if !is_known(engine, items[turn]) {
            let _ = ask(engine, items[turn])
            answered = answered + 1

    if times != null { eprintln(core_times(core, answered, times!)) }
    let _ = avra_cores_leave(group, core, answered, 0)
}

type CoreLearned = { high_words: List<int>, rows: List<LearnedRow>, inputs: List<LearnedRow>, stood: List<StoodRow> }

/// What a core learned and what stood in it, as it publishes them.
fn core_learned(learned: List<HeldEntry>, stood: List<HeldEntry>) -> CoreLearned {
    let sorted = sorted_by_hash(learned, (e: HeldEntry) -> e.question)
    CoreLearned {
        high_words: [e.question.high_word for e in sorted],
        rows: [row_of(e) for e in sorted],
        inputs: [row_of(e) for e in sorted if e.input],
        stood: [StoodRow { question: e.question, answer: e.answer } for e in stood],
    }
}
